name: HCL Technologies Ltd

segments.itbs: IT & Business Services: applications, infrastructure (cloud, digital workplace, networks), digital process operations (BPO), cybersecurity, data & AI; 73.8% of FY26 US$ revenue, EBIT 16.0%.
segments.ers: Engineering & R&D Services: software, embedded, mechanical, VLSI/silicon and platform engineering for product companies (tech, telecom, auto, medtech, semiconductors); 17.0% of FY26 revenue, EBIT 16.8%.
segments.sw: HCLSoftware: owned software products, largely acquired (select IBM software products in 2019, Actian data products, Zeenea, Jaspersoft): HCL DX, Unica, Commerce, BigFix, AppScan, Workload Automation, UnO, Actian Ingres and data intelligence. Sold as subscription & support (85% of FY26 segment revenue), perpetual licences (9%) and services (6%); 9.5% of revenue, EBIT 26.7%; ARR US$1.06 bn.
segments.src: AR FY26 note 3.30; Q4FY26 investor release (21-Apr-2026)

fy26.src: Q4FY26 investor release and call (21-Apr-2026); AR FY26

q1fy27.marginBridge: Reported EBIT +39 bp QoQ to 16.9%: lower restructuring +70 bp, lower doubtful-debt provision +20 bp, forex +60 bp, offset by -110 bp from annual productivity give-backs in managed-services contracts and the ERS decline (CFO).
callPoints: **Guidance unchanged:** FY27 revenue +1-4% CC (Services +1.5-4.5%), EBIT 17.5-18.5% including ~40-50 bp of restructuring; organic only (excludes Jaspersoft and HPE Telco Solutions). Management will revisit after Q2: the macro "we saw in March continues to be the same" (CEO).

**Bookings:** net new TCV US$2.41 bn, the highest ever first quarter, plus a mega deal with a Europe-headquartered Fortune Global 50 company (digital workplace and enterprise networks, US$1.14 bn per brokers) signed in early July; it reaches steady state only in April 2027, so FY27 revenue impact is negligible.

**AI:** Advanced AI revenue US$171 m (+10.6% QoQ, +62.1% YoY CC); AI Force deployed in 92 accounts (75 in Q4FY26); 23 industry AI solutions. Management's frame: AI-native and AI-amplified work grows; AI-disrupted traditional work keeps deflating.

**New bets:** an AI data-centre business (initial investment up to Rs3,500 cr, long-term ambition 50 MW, to be funded partly by partners, client commitments and debt, "not at the expense of our stated payout policy"), and a US$150 m strategic investment in Sarvam, an Indian sovereign-AI model company.

**Weak spots:** ERS fell 3.7% QoQ on cuts at two large US telecom clients and in Technology clients; Life Sciences & Healthcare is slow (end of regulatory work for medical-device clients; US healthcare under stress). HCLSoftware fell 5.3% YoY.

**Acquisitions:** Jaspersoft closed in the first week of July (US$10-15 m revenue a quarter); the HPE Telco Solutions carve-out was expected to close later in Q2 (it closed in August, HCLTech release dated 3-Aug-2026).
**People and cash:** headcount down 3,292 to 223,889; revenue per employee +3.3% YoY to US$65.5k; attrition 12.7%. LTM FCF US$1.98 bn (99% of net income); Rs12 interim dividend.

guidance.said: Revenue +3-5% CC, Services +3-5%, EBIT 17-18% (lowered from the 18-19% band given in Apr-2025, which analysts still call the "original 18-19%").
guidance.outcome: Revenue +3.9% CC; EBIT 17.2% including ~65 bp of restructuring (17.9% excluding it).

guidance.said: Services +4.75-5.25% CC, company +4-4.5% CC; EBIT 17-18% (incl. restructuring, excl. Labour Codes).
guidance.outcome: Missed slightly: company +3.9% (10 bp below the band) as software deals slipped and telecom clients cut spend in March.

guidance.said: Revenue +1-4% CC, Services +1.5-4.5%, EBIT 17.5-18.5% (incl. 40-50 bp restructuring); organic.
guidance.outcome: Q1: +2.6% YoY CC, EBIT 16.9% (17.5% ex restructuring); retained in July.

guidance.said: 40% of industry spend is AI-disrupted and can shrink 3-5% a year; for HCLTech's mix that is 2-3% a year; "very little" is in reported numbers yet, expected from FY27.
guidance.outcome: Too early to test; Q1 revenue per employee +3.3% while headcount fell.

guidance.said: Policy extended five years: at least 75% of net income returned to shareholders (89.9% paid over FY22-26).
Return to the old 18-19% band: will be addressed with FY28 guidance (CFO).

historySrc: Annual reports FY21-FY26; HCLTech press releases and investor calls; Deccan Herald / HCLTech releases on the HPE Telco Solutions and Jaspersoft deals

history.event: HCL group founded by Shiv Nadar and colleagues (2026 marks its 50th year); HCL Technologies Ltd incorporated in 1991 (CIN L74140DL1991PLC046369).
history.impact: Founder-family control through holding companies to this day.

history.event: Bought Actian (data management software) through a joint venture with Sumeru; minority bought out in FY22 for Rs746 cr.
history.impact: Start of the data-software portfolio inside HCLSoftware.

history.event: Acquisition of select IBM software products consummated on 30-Jun-2019; deferred consideration of Rs6,488 cr paid in FY21.
history.impact: Products & Platforms (now HCLSoftware) revenue rose from Rs8,115 cr (FY20) to Rs10,442 cr (FY21); D&A rose from Rs2,073 cr (FY19) to Rs4,611 cr (FY21) as the IP was amortised.
Share count doubled to 271.4 cr; per-share history is adjusted. Buybacks of 71.4 m shares in FY17-19.

history.event: Roshni Nadar Malhotra became Chairperson (she signs the FY21 annual report as Chairperson); Shiv Nadar retired as MD on 19-Jul-2021 and became Chairman Emeritus & Strategic Advisor. C Vijayakumar, CEO since 20-Oct-2016, became CEO & MD; re-appointed to Mar-2030 (AGM Aug-2025).
history.impact: Stable leadership; the family keeps control (60.9%).

history.event: Capital allocation policy introduced: at least 75% of net income returned over five years.
history.impact: Payout 84-98% since; HCLTech became a high-dividend stock (Rs60 a share in FY26).

history.event: Smaller buys in engineering and software (GBS banking software Jan-2022, ASAP Group automotive engineering FY24); HCLSoftware brand created.
history.impact: ERS grew from Rs13,564 cr (FY22) to Rs17,667 cr (FY24).

history.event: Divested its stake in the State Street HCL Services joint venture (Sep-2024; gain of Rs574 cr in other income); bought HPE's Communications Technology Group (2024).
history.impact: FY25 other income (Rs2,485 cr) was inflated by the one-off gain.

history.event: Restructuring programme (~65 bp of margin, Q2-Q4) and a one-time Rs956 cr charge for India's New Labour Codes (Q3); agreements to buy HPE's Telco Solutions business (~Rs1,400 cr) and Jaspersoft (US$240 m, Dec-2025), plus Wobby and Finergic.
history.impact: FY26 EBIT margin 17.2% (17.9% ex restructuring); reported EPS Rs61.33 vs Rs64.0 normalised.

history.event: US$150 m investment in Sarvam AI; AI data-centre business announced (up to Rs3,500 cr initially); Jaspersoft closed; US$1.14 bn mega deal signed; HPE Telco Solutions closed in Aug-2026.
history.impact: ~Rs5,000 cr of cash deployed in FY27 outside the core business; new capital-heavy line.
